title: Channel Adoption Pathways and Post-Adoption Behavior
authors: Shirsho Biswas, Hema Yoganarasimhan, Haonan Zhang
eligible_reason: No staggered adoption in any reported specification. Each of the three studies (Covid, Black Friday 2019, loyalty program 2023) is a separate 2x2 DiD in which every adopter is coded as treated from one common calendar month (May 2020, Dec 2019, Oct 2023) after dropping the adoption window; within each regression there is one adoption cohort. The adopter-vs-adopter comparisons (event vs organic pathway) use a time-invariant group interacted with a common Post. Not a near-miss: the design itself fails the two-cohort rule, independently of controls.
design_notes: Customer-month panels from one retailer. Static: feols(y ~ Treat_Post | CUSTOMER_ID + STARTOFMONTH, cluster = CUSTOMER_ID). Event studies: Treat x i(relative month, ref = -1) with the same FE, relative month defined from one common date. Loyalty study adds four time-varying activation controls (isActivated, FIRST_ACTIVATION_MONTH, MONTHS_SINCE_FIRST_ACTIVATION, FRACTION_OF_ACTIVATION_MONTH_SINCE_ACTIVATION) to every column. The loyalty forward-buying regression (line 426) realigns Jun-Sep 2023 online-adoption cohorts to event time with CUSTOMER_ID + EVENT_TIME FE. Covid and Black Friday files carry no individual adoption date (only Label and Post indicators); only the loyalty file has FIRST_ONLINE_DATE (adopters: Jun 849, Jul 975, Aug 17, Sep 159 in the 5% sample).
estimators_reported: TWFE event study around a common date
pooled OLS DiD without FE (printed alongside)
event-time FE regression on realigned cohorts
OLS linear trend on aggregated monthly series (Figure 3, notebook)
n_eligible_specs_note: All 28 recorded specifications use a single common treatment date within the regression.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: One cohort per regression: Covid adopters treated from May 2020, Black Friday adopters from Dec 2019, loyalty adopters from Oct 2023. The three studies are run on separate samples.

data_access: proprietary (NDA with the retailer; the public package ships a masked 5% random customer subsample with mean-zero normal noise added to spend and profit)
data_files: Data/1_Covid_Analysis_Data_Submission.csv (2,187,068 rows; 55,000 customers: 3,593 Covid, 1,407 organic, 50,000 offline-only; 2019-01 to 2023-04)
Data/2_BlackFriday_Analysis_Data_Submission.csv (966,714 rows; 52,000 customers: 599 Black Friday, 1,401 organic, 50,000 offline-only; 2019-01 to 2020-10)
Data/3_Loyalty_Analysis_Data_Submission.csv (717,897 rows; 49,110 customers: 176 loyalty, 1,824 organic, 47,110 offline-only; 2023-01 to 2024-03)
Data/*_Figure_1_Replication.csv and Data/4*_ShareOfflineSpend.csv (aggregates for Figures 1 and 3)
data_files_note: Fuzzed data. README and Alternative Disclosure Plan: 5% random, masked subsample; independent mean-zero normal noise added to spend and profit. Checks (read-only, pandas): TOTAL_VALUE_MONTH is below OFFLINE_VALUE_MONTH in 17-21% of rows and TOTAL_PROFIT_MONTH is negative in 29-32% of rows, consistent with additive noise; customer IDs are re-indexed. All published outcomes (spend, profit, share of offline spend with the noised spend denominator) are affected. Unbalanced panels.
data_provenance_note: Fuzzed (noise-added) 5% random subsample of NDA data. The subsampling alone would count as original data with a flag (PROTOCOL 5b), but the added noise on spend and profit places it in the fuzzed category, excluded from the main analysis. Moot here because no specification is eligible.
software_notes: R (fixest feols) for all DiD tables and event studies; Python notebook (statsmodels OLS) for Figures 1 and 3 only.
priority_note: Not eligible (single common treatment date in every regression) and data are fuzzed.
screener_notes: Screened from the package only; no article text in the project, so table and figure numbers come from the README and code comments and should be checked against the published article. No package code was run. A staggered design could in principle be built from FIRST_ONLINE_DATE in the loyalty file (four monthly cohorts), but the authors never estimate one, so it does not count. The Dataverse listing in the scoping report ('four pathways') corresponds to three event studies plus the organic pathway used as a comparison group.
main_text_note: AAM checked: Eq. (1) y_it = customer FE + month FE + beta0 I{Post_t} x I{Adopter_i} (+ loyalty-program controls) and Eq. (2) with I{Event Adopter_i} x I{Post_t}; I{Post_t} is a calendar pre/post split per event (Table 3), so each regression has one adoption cohort. Main-text DiD tables: Table 5 (spend, adopters vs offline-only), Table 6 (profit), Table 7 (spend, event vs organic adopters), Table 8 (share of offline spend), Table 10 (profit, event vs organic); columns COVID-19, Black Friday, Loyalty Program. Figure 2 (forward buying: (a) Black Friday, (b) Loyalty Program), Figure 4 (COVID-19 pre-trends: (b)(c) spend, (e)(f) profit), Figure 5 HonestDiD. A doubly robust DiD (did package) for the COVID analysis is in the Web Appendix only (Table A30), again with one cohort.
screener_notes_nov2: Re-checked Nov 2 under the Nov 1 coding rule: no change. 3_Loyalty_Analysis_Submission.R drops Jun-Sep 2023 (lines 51, 181, 277) and sets TreatedMonth = 2023-10-01 for every adopter (lines 186, 272), so each regression has one adoption cohort; Covid and Black Friday studies likewise use one common post date. eligible_design = false and near_miss = false are consistent with the rule (a single-cohort design is not a staggered near-miss). Package was downloaded Nov 1 (md5 matched) and not re-downloaded.
